models.summary: The implicit deflator compares current-price GDP with real GDP for the same output; dividing nominal GDP by the ratio recovers real GDP.

relationship.locator: Learning Module3, Nominal and Real GDP, printed pp129-130 (PDF pp141-142), unnumbered GDP deflator and realGDP equations

models.title: Value added by a production stage
models.summary: Value added removes intermediate input value from a stage output value so aggregation across stages avoids counting intermediate production repeatedly.

relationship.original_equation: Value added = sales/output value minus purchased intermediate inputs
relationship.locator: Learning Module3, Gross Domestic Product / Value Added, printed pp125-127 (PDF pp137-139), Exhibit2 and Example1
relationship.translation_notes: Currency minus currency yields currency. This is a production-account concept, distinct from gross profit, whose cost-of-sales scope need not equal intermediate consumption. Receipts in the simplified source example proxy output value; inventories require the full output definition.

variables.definition: Gross output value produced by the stage over the measurement period
variables.context: Same domestic economy, accounting period and annualization basis; current-price flows unless explicitly marked constant-price; one currency without exchange conversion

variables.definition: Purchased intermediate goods and services consumed in producing that output; excludes labor and capital income
variables.context: Same domestic economy, accounting period and annualization basis; current-price flows unless explicitly marked constant-price; one currency without exchange conversion

variables.definition: Gross value added by that stage on the consistent valuation basis
variables.context: Same domestic economy, accounting period and annualization basis; current-price flows unless explicitly marked constant-price; one currency without exchange conversion

assumptions: Source assumption: gross output and intermediate inputs use consistent valuation and accounting periods.
Source assumption: inputs are consumed intermediate production, rather than capital expenditures or factor payments.
limitations: Negative value added is mathematically and economically possible; it is not silently clipped. Full GDP aggregation also needs valuation adjustments and domestic coverage.
